question.text: Saraswati Cat II AIF reports a Kaplan-Schoar Public Market Equivalent (KS-PME) of 1.35 against the NIFTY 500 TRI, and a Direct Alpha of +6.2% p.a. The Fund Manager, Ms. Priya Deshpande, wants to explain to LPs what these numbers mean. Which interpretation is correct?

answer.text: KS-PME > 1 means the fund UNDERPERFORMED the public market; the +6.2% Direct Alpha contradicts it and one number must be wrong.
KS-PME = 1.35 means the fund beat NIFTY 500 TRI by 35 basis points; Direct Alpha of 6.2% is unrelated.

KS-PME = 1.35 means for every INR 1 invested in NIFTY 500 TRI at the same cash-flow timing, the AIF returned INR 1.35 of equivalent value — i.e., the fund OUTPERFORMED the public market; Direct Alpha of +6.2% is the annualised excess return that confirms this.
KS-PME is always > 1 by construction and carries no interpretive content; only Direct Alpha matters.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 10.8 / Ch 9.8.5: KS-PME > 1 means the AIF outperformed the public market benchmark (the AIF turned the same cash-flow stream into more value than the index would have). KS-PME < 1 = underperformed. Direct Alpha converts PME into an annualised excess-return number — here +6.2% p.a. over the NIFTY 500 TRI. The two measures are consistent (both positive). The Trap: Option A inverts the threshold. Option B confuses the multiplicative ratio (1.35 = 35% premium) with 35 bps. Option D is false — KS-PME can be anywhere on the real line.
